advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Install scc in the CI test job (or a dedicated code-health job) so the integration-tier `skipif(shutil.which('scc') is None)` reconciliation/AC5 tests actually execute rather than skipping on every CI run.
evidence: tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc_heldout.py:207 `@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("scc") is None, reason="scc is not installed")` guarding test_live_scan_root_with_files_never_reports_a_confident_zero (AC5), test_live_reported_loc_matches_wc_l (AC4), test_live_include_extensions_excludes_assets_and_resources (AC3)

tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_module_size_reconciliation_heldout.py:83 and :95 same skipif guard on test_metric_file_set_and_loc_match_the_ci_gate and test_configured_scan_excludes_bundled_assets_and_resource_wordlists
.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:536 the integration tier IS run in CI: `Run the integration tier` -> `pytest -m integration`
.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:278 the only install step is `uv sync --locked --extra dev` — no scc install; a search for 'scc' across .github/ returns no matches

ABSENCE: the property that scc's `Lines` actually equals `wc -l` on this tree and that `--include-ext` actually excludes the interleaved assets is asserted ONLY by these scc-requiring tests, so it is never verified in CI
advisory.finding: The ticket's load-bearing regression assertions against REAL scc (AC5 confident-zero regression, AC4 exact `wc -l` reconciliation, AC3 real-tool asset exclusion) never gate in CI: they are `@pytest.mark.integration @pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which('scc') is None)`, the integration tier runs in CI, but no CI job installs scc.
scenarios: A future scc version changes `Lines` semantics or the `--include-ext` behavior; the metric silently diverges from the CI module-size gate and no CI test catches it.
The AC5 confident-zero regression at the real-adapter level is never re-run in CI, so a real-scc-specific regression reappears undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an scc install step (e.g. `go install github.com/boyter/scc/v3@<pin>` or the release binary) to the pytest job in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml so the integration tier exercises the real tool; otherwise document why real-scc reconciliation is intentionally dev-only.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test that builds a metrics ctx with `include_extensions` set and asserts (a) scc_loc.analyze receives it and (b) two runs with different include_extensions get distinct analysis-cache entries (no stale reuse).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:199-212 adds `getattr(ctx, 'include_extensions', ())`, conditional threading into scc_loc.analyze, and `_cached_analysis(ctx, 'scc', (scan_roots, extensions), analyze)` with the comment 'two differently narrowed runs ... must not share a cached result'

search across tests for `include_extensions=` returns only tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc_heldout.py (calls scc_loc.analyze directly) and test_scc_module_size_reconciliation_heldout.py (calls scc_loc.analyze directly, and is scc-gated)

tests/unit/metrics/test_code_health_composition.py:54 and test_git_metrics_heldout.py:75 build the ctx SimpleNamespace WITHOUT an include_extensions attribute, so the getattr default path is what runs — the configured path is never exercised

ABSENCE: no test constructs a ctx with include_extensions set and asserts (a) the extension reaches scc_loc.analyze, or (b) two ctx runs with different include_extensions produce distinct cache entries rather than colliding
advisory.finding: The new `include_extensions` threading through `git_metrics._scc_analysis` (passing it to scc_loc.analyze) and the cache-key expansion `(scan_roots, extensions)` have no CI-runnable test: the only tests that set include_extensions call `scc_loc.analyze` directly (bypassing git_metrics) or require real scc.
scenarios: A refactor drops `extensions` from the cache key tuple; two differently-narrowed projects (or a re-run after config change) silently reuse a stale cached file set and no CI test fails.
The `getattr(ctx, 'include_extensions', ())` threading is broken so the configured extension never reaches scc; caught only by the scc-requiring integration tests, which skip in CI.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics_heldout.py, monkeypatch scc_loc.analyze to record its kwargs, evaluate the module-size spec against a SimpleNamespace ctx with include_extensions=('py',) and then include_extensions=('go',) sharing one analysis_cache, and assert analyze was called twice with the respective extensions (proving both threading and the cache-key split).
